pages.title: Backport Overview
pages.text: $(thing)TerraFirmaEarth$() brings major world content from newer TFC versions back to Minecraft 1.20.1 Forge. This section covers only backported content; TFE-original features and redesigned systems are kept in New Features and Reworked Systems.

pages.title: Backport Scope
pages.text: The backport includes 109 terrain biomes, 31 climate types, newer seasonal and snow behavior, seasonal plants, crops, weeds and flowers, new fauna and pests, and newer devices such as the stove.

pages.title: Backported Terrain
pages.text: TFE brings the full terrain biome and transition system from newer TFC versions to 1.20, for a current total of 109 landforms. Temperature, rainfall, distance from the coast, hotspot age, and rock conditions combine to select them.

pages.title: Major Terrain Families
pages.text: Coasts and oceans include bays, tidal flats, rocky shores, sea stacks, reefs, deep oceans, and trenches. Land includes badlands, canyons, mesas, dune seas, salt flats, karst lakes, and sinkholes. Cold and high-energy terrain includes staged volcanoes, ice sheets, subglacial lakes, glacial mountains, and eroded glacial landforms.

pages.title: Generation Note
pages.text: Terrain biomes appear only in newly generated chunks. Many similarly named biomes form continuous transitions rather than isolated attractions, so traveling in one direction may cross several stages of the same terrain family.

pages.title: Backported Climate and Seasons
pages.text: TFE brings 31 newer climate types, the newer Climate screen and Calendar display, and northern/southern seasonal behavior to 1.20. Players can see annual mean and current temperature plus average and current rainfall, while ecology and weather use the appropriate reading.

pages.title: Hemispheres and Elevation
pages.text: The default temperature scale is 20,000 blocks, making the latitude distance from equator to pole about 20,000 blocks. Seasons are six months apart between hemispheres. Above Y=63, surface temperature falls by about 0.16225°C per block, up to roughly 17.822°C.

pages.title: Snow and Seasonal Plants
pages.text: Snow accumulation and melting catch up promptly in the matching climate instead of requiring a long wait after entering an area. Leaves, flowers, lotus, sunflowers, and other plants change appearance with the season, while server ecology still uses the hemisphere of the plant's own position.

pages.title: Backported Plants and Crops
pages.text: TFE brings plants, wild flowers and grasses, weeds, farmland flowers, and crops from newer versions to 1.20, including working seasonal models. Normal, dead, wild, and aquatic plants also receive the appropriate tool, snow, ice, and plant classifications.

pages.title: Six Crops
pages.text: The backported crops are cassava, lentil, peanut, alfalfa, canola, and radish. They include natural generation, seeds, mature harvests, food data, tool harvesting, and guide pages while retaining 1.20's single primary nutrient system. See New Crop Adjustments in Reworked Systems for their climate values.

pages.title: Backported Fauna and Pests
pages.text: TFE brings newer climate fauna and spawning conditions to 1.20. New animals such as bison and leopard seals use newer biome and climate rules, while existing animals such as polar bears and dire wolves also use the newer temperature, groundwater, and biome ranges.

pages.title: Pest System
pages.text: Lemmings, mongooses, and jerboas use climate-driven pest rules rather than ordinary animal spawning. When the environment is suitable, they can appear as the matching pests; not finding them in an ordinary spawn list does not mean they were omitted.

pages.title: Backported Devices and Compatibility
pages.text: Some newer content cannot be placed directly into 1.20. TFE adapts the items, blocks, visuals, and world content already present there so backported plants, climate, devices, and terrain work together in the same Forge environment.

pages.title: Stove
pages.text: A $(thing)Stove$() is a variant of the $(thing)Firepit$() that can be used without the fear of it setting nearby blocks on fire. It has all the same functionality as a firepit, and a pot can be added as well. However, a grill cannot be added to the Stove.
